The question was matched to: material flammability. Below is what the indexed documents state about it, quoted with their sources.

**Evidence**
- Concurrent Flame Spread Modeling using Flamelet Generated Manifolds in Microgravity with Comparison to BASS Experiments using Two-Color Tomography: Microgravity flammability boundary for PMMA rods in axial stagnation flow: Experimental results and energy balance analyses (2017); Radiative flamelet generated manifolds for solid fuel flame spread in microgravity (2023); Theoretical estimates of flammability bounds for thin… [S1]
- BASS: Flame spread and extinction over realistic solid fuels (cotton-fiberglass fabric, PMMA in several geometries, Nomex) in low-speed forced flow aboard the ISS. Built to bridge the gap between the 1-g NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 screening method and real microgravity flammability, and… [S2]
- SAFFIRE-I: gravity material flammability screening test. [S3]
- SAFFIRE-III: (1) determine how rapidly a large scale fire grows in low-gravity and (2) investigate the low-g flammability limits compared to those obtained in NASA’s normal gravity material flammability screening test. [S4]
- SAFFIRE-II: Buoyant Effects on the Flammability of Silicone Samples Planned for the Spacecraft Fire Experiment (Saffire), Conference: 45th International Conference on Environmental Systems ICES-2015-[293] 12-16 July 2015, Bellevue, Washington; The Spacecraft Fire Experiment (Saffire) -… [S5]
- Microgravity and 1-g rankings of materials can disagree: In SAFFIRE-II, 4 of 4 silicone samples (0.27–1.03 mm) had a burn length of about 0 in microgravity at 20 cm/s, while 2 of the 4 matching 1-g reference burns were complete. Flames did spread in microgravity over: PMMA, SIBAL (cotton-fibergla [S10]
- Scale matters: only SAFFIRE burned spacecraft-size samples: SAFFIRE-I and -III burned ~0.4 m × 0.94 m fabric samples in uncrewed Cygnus vehicles, with O2/CO2, pressure, temperature and flame-growth measurements — the only realistic-scale fire data in PSI. Limitation: Two samples per mission, one mat [S11]

- Only documents in this knowledge base were searched.

sources.title: BASS-II — Burning and Suppression of Solids - II — insight:bass2-reduced-o2
sources.text: BASS-II maps solid-fuel burning down to 13.6 % O2. BASS-II ran 129 tests with initial O2 between 13.6 and 22.2 % vol, mostly on PMMA, SIBAL (cotton-fiberglass fabric), Nomex. Flow annotations record extinction in 15 tests, blow-off in 3 and no ignition in 1. What O2 and flow combinations define the flammability boundary of common cabin plastics in microgravity?

sources.text: SAFFIRE-I and -III burned ~0.4 m × 0.94 m fabric samples in uncrewed Cygnus vehicles, with O2/CO2, pressure, temperature and flame-growth measurements — the only realistic-scale fire data in PSI. Limitation: Two samples per mission, one material (SIBAL).

sources.title: BASS-II maps solid-fuel burning down to 13.6 % O2
sources.text: BASS-II ran 129 tests with initial O2 between 13.6 and 22.2 % vol, mostly on PMMA, SIBAL (cotton-fiberglass fabric), Nomex. Flow annotations record extinction in 15 tests, blow-off in 3 and no ignition in 1. Limitation: Outcome annotations are free text; flow units to be confirmed in the BASS-II documentation; flame-spread rates are in the raw video data.

sources.title: 1-g material screening is not automatically conservative
sources.text: Spacecraft material selection relies on NASA-STD-6001 Test 1, which ranks materials by 1-g behaviour. BASS and BASS-II were built on the hypothesis that, with adequate ventilation, materials burn as well if not better in microgravity than in normal gravity. Limitation: Specific materials and geometries; flow and O2 per test partly only in raw files for BASS.

top_passage.text: The objective of this ground investigation was to use flight data obtained from PSI through NASA’s Flame Extinguishment Experiment (FLEX) to quantify how externally imposed thermal and convective perturbations regulated the dynamics and ultimate fate of already established droplet cool flames, and to explain run-to-run variability by isolating the roles of deliberate heating and unintentional drift-induced convection. Focusing on both small and large droplets, the work mapped stability windows for ignition, sustained oscillation, transitions to hot ignition and warm-flame behavior, and extinction under microgravity.
